decision_conditions: Reason : 1 - The proposed use of the property as a House in Multiple Occupation is unacceptable in principle due to its location within an area with a Public Transport Accessibility Level (PTAL) of 1B, which represents poor access to public transport. In the absence of a parking stress survey, as required by the Houses in Multiple Occupation Supplementary Planning Document for proposals in low-accessibility areas, the applicant has failed to demonstrate that the development would not result in unacceptable pressure on on-street parking or promote unsustainable travel patterns. The proposal is therefore contrary to Local Plan Policy SC10 and the Houses in Multiple Occupation SPD.

Reason : 2 - The proposed development is unacceptable in principle as the application site is not located within convenient walking distance (400m) of Metropolitan or District town centre facilities. The proposal therefore fails to direct higher-intensity residential uses to accessible and sustainable locations, contrary to the locational requirements of Local Plan Policy SC10 and the Houses in Multiple Occupation Supplementary Planning Document.

Reason : 3 - The proposed conversion of the property to a House in Multiple Occupation is unacceptable in principle as the original, non-extended floor area of the dwelling is below 130 square metres, is not considered suitable for conversion to an HMO under Local Plan Policy SC10 and the Houses in Multiple Occupation Supplementary Planning Document. As such, the property, and the proposal is contrary to the development plan.

Reason : 4 - The proposal has failed to demonstrate that the use of the property as a House in Multiple Occupation, either individually or cumulatively with other similar uses in the surrounding area, would not result in unacceptable harm to residential amenity. In the absence of evidence relating to existing HMO concentrations, mitigation measures, or effective management arrangements, it cannot be concluded that the proposal would not result in increased disturbance, noise, and activity detrimental to neighbouring occupiers. The proposal is therefore contrary to Local Plan Policy SC10 and the Houses in Multiple Occupation Supplementary Planning Document.

Reason : 5 - The proposal would result in the substandard provision of outdoor amenity space, and the siting of cycle storage sheds and refuse storage within the rear garden would further reduce the amount of usable amenity space available to occupiers. In addition, the proposal fails to provide a dedicated clothes-drying area, either externally or internally, as required by the Houses in Multiple Occupation Supplementary Planning Document. As such, the proposal would fail to provide an adequate standard of amenity for future occupiers and is contrary to Local Plan Policy SC5 and the Houses in Multiple Occupation SPD.

Reason : 6 - The proposed use of the property as a House in Multiple Occupation would result in an unacceptable impact on the living conditions of neighbouring occupiers, by virtue of the increased comings and goings, noise, and associated disturbance. Considering the sustained history of complaints relating to noise nuisance, anti-social behaviour, and poor management of the premises, and in the absence of robust mitigation or management measures, it has not been demonstrated that the proposal would adequately safeguard residential amenity. The proposal is therefore contrary to Local Plan Policy SC10 and the Houses in Multiple Occupation Supplementary Planning Guidance.

Reason : 7 - The proposal fails to demonstrate that appropriate provision for the storage and collection of refuse and recycling, as required for Houses in Multiple Occupation. While a refuse storage area is indicated on the Location Plan, no details have been provided, or an appropriate waste management strategy for the property. The proposal is therefore contrary to Local Plan Policies SC10 and EQ7, the Houses in Multiple Occupation Supplementary Planning Document, and the Council's Recycling and Refuse Guidance.
description: Retrospective application for the change of use from a single dwellinghouse (Use Class C3) to a 6-bedroom 6-person House in Multiple Occupation (Use Class C4).
